docs.summary: AudioSource component for playing audio in the scene. Supports spatial audio, effects, procedural generation, and serialization.
The mixer group this source feeds into, or null to go straight to the master output. Setting it re-routes immediately, so a running source moves buses without restarting.
How many one shot voices this source can sound at once before stealing the oldest. Lowering it takes voices away immediately rather than waiting for them to finish.

Raised for every block this source produces, after its effects have run, on the audio thread. A handler must not allocate, block or touch the scene: it is running against the mix, where a collection or a contended lock is an audible dropout.
docs.remarks: Subscribing builds the node that runs the chain if this source did not already have one, so a source nobody is listening to and that has no effects does not pay for either.

docs.summary: The clip this source plays. Assigning a different one stops playback, since what was playing was the previous clip. Starting the new one is [`Play`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~Play)'s job.
If true, the audio will start playing automatically when OnEnable is called.
If true, the audio will loop continuously.
The slowest playback speed a source can be set to. Zero stalls the resampler and a negative rate is not something the native layer defines, so the range stops short of both.

Level of the audio source. 1 is the clip as it was authored, 0 is silence, and above 1 amplifies. Negative is not a quieter sound, it is the same sound with its phase inverted, so the range stops at 0.
Playback speed of the audio source, which carries the pitch with it. 1 is the clip's own rate. Never below [`MinPitch`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~MinPitch).
Stereo pan of the audio source (-1.0 left, 0.0 center, 1.0 right).
Pan mode (Balance or Pan).
If true, spatial audio (3D positioning) is enabled.
Strength of the pitch shift from relative motion. 0 disables doppler, 1 is the real world amount, and above that exaggerates it. Never negative, which would shift the wrong way.
Distance below which the source plays at full volume. Never negative, and never past [`MaxDistance`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~MaxDistance), which is carried up with it if need be.
Distance at which the source reaches its quietest. Never below [`MinDistance`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~MinDistance).
Attenuation model for spatial audio distance falloff.
Returns true if the audio source is currently playing.
Playback position, counted in the frames the device runs at.
docs.remarks: This is the engine's own read position, so it advances at the rate the device was opened at whatever rate the clip was authored at. That is not the unit [`Length`](#api~Prowl.Scaffold.Length) is in, so the two do not belong in one expression. [`NormalizedTime`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~NormalizedTime) is what compares them. It also keeps counting across a loop rather than starting over, so on a looping source it is how long the source has been sounding for. [`PlaybackTime`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~PlaybackTime) is where in the clip it currently is.

docs.summary: Length of the playing clip, counted in the frames it was authored at.
docs.remarks: This comes from the decoder rather than from the mix, so it is in the clip's own rate. Only a clip that happens to have been authored at the rate the device was opened at counts the same way [`Cursor`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~Cursor) does.

docs.summary: Where in the clip playback currently is, in seconds. Named to stay clear of the engine's [`Time`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Time) class.
Length of the playing clip in seconds, 0 when nothing is loaded.
Playback position as a fraction of the clip, 0 at the start and 1 at the end.
docs.remarks: Compared as seconds, because the two frame counts are not counted at the same rate. Dividing one by the other answers the ratio between those rates as much as it answers the position: a clip authored at half the rate the device runs at reached 1 barely half way through.

docs.summary: Called when the object becomes enabled and active. Only called when the GameObject is in a Scene and enabled.
Called every frame.

The attenuation range, so the falloff can be placed against the scene rather than guessed at from two numbers in the inspector. Only while selected: a scene full of emitters would be unreadable otherwise.
The inspector writes the backing fields directly, so the native side has to be re-synced from them rather than from the property setters.
Called when the object becomes disabled or inactive. Only called when the GameObject was in a Scene and becomes disabled.
Called when the Component will be destroyed. This is an override of EngineObject.OnDispose() and is also exposed as a virtual lifecycle method.
Plays the assigned AudioClip.
Plays procedurally generated audio using the Read event callback.
Stops playback and rewinds to the start. Use [`Pause`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~Pause) to stop without losing the position.
Stops playback while remembering the position, so [`Resume`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~Resume) picks up where it left off. Does nothing if the source is not playing.
Continues from where [`Pause`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~Pause) stopped. Does nothing if the source is not paused.
docs.remarks: The position is restored explicitly after starting rather than relying on the stopped source having kept it, so this behaves the same whether the native layer rewinds on stop or not.

docs.summary: True while [`Pause`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~Pause) is holding the position for a later [`Resume`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~Resume).

members.name: PlayOneShot
members.signature: public void PlayOneShot(AudioClip clip, float volumeScale = 1.0f)

docs.summary: Plays a clip on its own voice, without disturbing whatever this source is already playing. Overlapping calls layer instead of cutting each other off, which is what a one shot is for.
docs.remarks: Voices are pooled and share the source's sound group, so they inherit its volume, pitch and spatial settings and follow the object as it moves. Once [`MaxOneShotVoices`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~MaxOneShotVoices) are sounding at once the longest running one is taken over.

params.volumeScale: Level for this voice alone, on top of the source's own volume.

docs.summary: Stops every one shot voice this source is sounding. Leaves the main playback alone.
How many one shot voices are sounding right now.

members.name: PlayClipAtPoint
members.signature: public static AudioSource PlayClipAtPoint(AudioClip clip, Float3 position, float volume = 1.0f)

docs.summary: Plays a clip at a world position with no emitter of its own, for sounds whose source is gone by the time they finish, like an impact or a pickup. Returns null if there is no scene to put it in.
The effect chain, in processing order.

Adds an audio effect to the processing chain. The source takes ownership: the effect is destroyed when it is removed from the chain or when the source itself is destroyed. Disabling and re-enabling the source keeps the chain intact.
Removes an audio effect from the processing chain and destroys it.
Removes an audio effect by index and destroys it.
Removes and destroys every audio effect in the chain.
Binds every effect to the current audio format and republishes the chain the audio thread reads. Call after editing [`Effects`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.AudioSource~Effects) in place.
Gets the number of active effects.
The world space velocity the doppler shift is being driven from, in units per real second.
docs.remarks: This used to difference the sound group's position against the previous position that Update had already overwritten with it, so it always answered roughly zero, and divided by a delta it never checked. It now reports the value Update actually handed the audio engine.

docs.summary: Gets the output buffer after effect processing (useful for FFT analysis).
Called right after this component is deserialized, before any lifecycle callback. Override to react to freshly loaded values.
